text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South African customs investigators are due in the capital Windhoek next week to discuss an alledged smuggling scam involving Namibian and South African companies, estimated to involve more than two billion rand.

- Namibian Minerals Corporation, already active in Namibia and South Africa, says it has now acquired a minimum 42 percent interest in three diamond concessions in Angola, and a 70 percent stake in ten exploration licenses and a mining permit in Zaire.

- DTA opposition leader Mishake Muyongo has continued to attack the proposed Local Authorities Amendment Act saying the ruling SWAPO party is only paying lip service to democracy. The amendment will provide for December local elections to be held on a party list system instead of the current ward system.
